newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn moves to broaden shareholder rights.
newsitem.headline: Bonn moves to broaden shareholder rights.

text.p: The German Justice Ministry on Tuesday unveiled legislative plans to broaden shareholder rights and increase transparency and corporate accountability.
"We must orient our corporate law more strongly toward international capital markets," Justice Minister Edzard Schmidt-Jortzig said in a statement.
The moves are an attempt to improve Germany's shareholder culture, in which banks are now seen to exercise great power at the expense of small shareholders.

The draft legislation would ease rules on corporate share buybacks in line with European Union guidelines, and limit banks' ability to exercise proxies on shares deposited with them, the statement said.
In line with Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition agreement, the government also plans to eliminate the multiple voting rights enjoyed by some shareholders, and the ceilings on maximum voting rights.
As a takeover defence, some companies now limit the voting rights a single shareholder may exercise, even if he holds more shares.
The draft law would also sharpen Bonn's supervision of companies' supervisory boards and limit the number of such posts a single director may hold.
